chapter: Teens, stride pianists and the Louisiana Stompers
title: Why he became a musician; piano battles in Harlem studios
summary: Piano beat grocery and tailor jobs as a livelihood; he describes the Cave and Jack and Jill studios, piano battles, and social-club work at Dunbar and the Renaissance.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You asked me what made me go into playing piano, to be a musician. It was better than working in a grocery store, or delivering suits at a tailor, a place... Like, we had the Spotless Cleaners and the Burger Service and things like that, you know. I done that also. Then I found that it was more to my liking. Then back in my teens I also had jobs at a furrier. Of course, even in the summertime, I tried that, when there's no school... The only thing about it, like, the boss was say, "Roger, on your way home drop these packages off." I wouldn't get home until 7 o'clock that night! And then I can remember going into the cold storage in the summertime; you'd have to put on an overcoat in there!

Anyhow, playing piano was a little more so to my liking as a livelihood, you know. So I got to make some extra money. And then I saw everybody was doing that. I met fellows playing violin, the saxophone...
Well, this was in different places in Harlem. One place called the Cave. We had the Black and Gold

Studio, the Jack and Jill Studios. Different places where the youngsters used to meet. And therefore, there was always a piano player, and then everybody that played piano would be around. "Well, So-and-So is going to be here, he's going to play," and "So-and-so is going to play here." And then there would be piano battles.
What date do you think we're talking about now?
Mmm, this is around the early Thirties.
The Louisiana Stompers are the early Thirties...
Well, it could happen at the same time.

Because, you know, Dunbar Palace we'd play on weekends, maybe a day, or maybe a dance... They had many social clubs in those days. And at the Renaissance, I mean, you had... Vernon always had a dancing band. He had Metcalf, he had Roy Eldridge...
